anatomy.status: ASSUMED anatomical constants, ~5% population spread. Everything that varies with the individual -- px per mm, gaze, aperture -- is measured from the plate.

world_axes: +X right, +Y away from camera, +Z up; actor centred at Y=0 (identical to make_proxy_mesh.py, on purpose)

proxy_projection_error_px.meaning: distance between the iris centre and the projection of the proxy vertex used as the corneal apex. Large values mean the mesh and the landmarks disagree about where the eye is, and the catchlight will sit off it.

plate_glint.clipping_note: an unclipped glint still has the iris diffuse recorded underneath it, so separate_specular.py can subtract it and leave real photographed texture. A clipped one cannot be recovered at all.

triangulation.why: the two corneas are ~63 mm apart, so for any source beyond a few tens of centimetres the rays are near parallel and the least-squares point collapses onto the corneas themselves WITH A SMALL RESIDUAL. A residual test alone passes on that nonsense; this gate is reach over baseline.

plate_key_light.direction_is_the_usable_output: mean_direction_world and its spread are the measurement to consume. The spread is not pure noise: both eyes see the same source, so genuine parallax between the two corneas inflates it when the source is near.
plate_key_light.why_it_matters: This is the only place in the frame where the plate photographed its own light sources directly. estimate_source_light.py fits SH to a surface whose normals all have ny < 0 and its own log warns that the resulting direction is an extrapolation; this is not.
